conclusion:
NOTHING in the crate's tables changes on this evidence alone; what changes is what may now be asserted, and one comment that is now provably too weak.

1. The literal question is closed as a hard negative. Under sgx.com/wps/portal/sgxweb/home/products/derivatives/equity/… the Nikkei 225 leaf is first archived 2021-05-06 and the MSCI Singapore leaf 2021-05-06 (also 2021-06-19); the 2013-08-20 FTSE China A50 leaf is the ONLY pre-2020 equity-index specification leaf in the whole subtree (69 pre-2020 rows). The derivatives Trading Hours page has exactly one 2010–2016 capture with content, the 2013-08-20 one already cited. So no in-era artifact states the Japan or Singapore pre-opening routine's length, and none exists to be found in these channels.

2. eras.rs's two "#65" sentences should be sharpened. They currently read "no artifact of this era that has been read states the pre-opening routine's length (#65)". After this sweep the stronger and now-true statement is available: no artifact of this era exists — the leaves were never archived, and the one in-era page that does survive (2013-08-20) states in SGX's own words that "All equity index futures and interest rate futures contracts are subject to a pre-opening routine and non-cancel period before the start of the T session and T+1 session" while giving no length and pointing the reader at specifications the archive does not hold. That is exactly the discipline AGENTS.md's "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists'" demands: the predecessor channels have now actually been searched, so the reason may be stated as a fact rather than as a limit on reading.

3. A genuinely new SGX-authored source class was found and it does state both routines — SGX's pre-portal `psv` contract-specification pages (sgx.com/psv/derivatives/futures_options/equity_index/*.shtml), captured 2006 to 2009-03-27 and never again. On the exact T bounds the two floor eras serve, SGX states: Nikkei 225 "Pre -Opening 7.30am -7.43 am / Non -Cancel Period 7.43am -7.45 am / Opening 7.45 am - 2.25 pm"; MSCI Singapore and Straits Times "Pre -Opening 8.15am -8.28 am / Non -Cancel Period 8.28am -8.30 am / Opening 8.30am-5.10 pm". Both are below the January-2010 floor, so this is not a revision row and not a carry-back — carry-back extends the earliest sourced state backwards, and these run forwards. The available move is the one history.rs already makes for 2020→2024 under #64: carry a routine forward over an interval in which no source states a change. Its warrant here is unusually strong, because the routine is demonstrably anchored to the open at a fixed 13+2 minutes across every product and every era SGX ever printed — A50 9.00-9.13/9.13-9.15 before a 9.15 open in 2009 and 8.45-8.58/8.58-9.00 before a 9.00 open in 2013; MSCI Taiwan 8.30-8.43/8.43-8.45 before an 8.45 open in 2009; Japan 7.15-7.28/7.28-7.30 before a 7.30 open in 2019-2020 — and because SiMSCI's T pre-open window 8.15-8.28/8.28-8.30 is literally unchanged from 2009 to the 2020 content-API payload.

   If the maintainer takes that decision, it is a two-line edit and nothing else moves: SGX_JAPAN_FLOOR gains order_entry: [(7, 30, 7, 45)] and SGX_SINGAPORE_FLOOR gains order_entry: [(8, 15, 8, 30)] — the Pre-Opening and Non-Cancel pair served as one order-entry window, exactly as the 2020 rows are built. Both are `order_entry` windows, which AGENTS.md's "Executable windows are the priority" places in the lower-stakes class: they change only whether orders could be queued ahead of an open that is itself modelled correctly.

4. The T+1 pre-open must stay unserved on both floor keys, and #65 stays open for that half. The 2009 pages put the Nikkei T+1 opening at 3.30 pm and the A50's at 3.40 pm and MSCI Taiwan's at 2.45 pm, against the 2013-08-20 table's 3.15pm, 4.40pm and 2.35pm; the table's own Notes say "All timings exclude pre-opening and pre-closing routines", so those are real opens and the T+1 anchor moved. Only SiMSCI's T+1 open (6.15 pm) is identical in both, so a carry-forward argument would be available for Singapore's T+1 queue (18:00–18:15) and not for Japan's — a split that should be decided explicitly rather than fall out of a table edit.

5. Two new lower bounds on state W belong beside the table, under LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES's requirement that the ordering argument be sourced. history.rs dates W's content to "about 2012" from its contract set alone. SGX's own 2009 pages now bound it from below on two rows: the Straits Times future opened 8.30 am in February 2009, so W's 07:55 STI open post-dates March 2009; and the A50 ran a lunch break (9.15-11.35, 1.00-3.05) in February 2009 and none in W. Neither is a dated cutover and neither should become one; they are recorded because they show W is not uniformly the oldest state row by row, which is the assumption the W-before-S0 ordering leans on.

6. Nothing here touches LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: no new date is asserted, no revision row is proposed, and every boundary in the branch stands as keyed.
